notes.text: The mourning — Which was seven days. Nor could the nature of the thing admit of longer delay, lest the too early birth of the child might discover David's sin. Bare a son - By which it appears, That David continued in the state of impenitency for divers months together; and this notwithstanding his frequent attendance upon God's ordinances. Which is an eminent instance of the corruption of man's nature, of the deceitfulness of sin, and of the tremendous judgment of God in punishing one sin, by delivering a man up to another. Nathan delivers and applies his parable, ver. 1-12. David repents and is forgiven, but punished, ver. 13. 14. The sickness and death of the child, with David's behaviour on the occasion, ver. 15-23. The birth of Solomon, ver. 24-25. The taking of Rabbah, ver. 26-31.

The Lord sent — When the ordinary means did not awaken David to repentance, God takes an extraordinary course. Thus the merciful God pities and prevents him who had so horribly forsaken God. He said - He prudently ushers in his reproof with a parable, after the manner of the eastern nations, that so he might surprize David, and cause him unawares to give sentence against himself.
Many flocks — Noting David's many wives and concubines.
Bought — As men then used to buy their wives: or, had procured.

Is worthy to die — This seems to be more than the fact deserved, or than he had commission to inflict for it, Exod. xxii, 1. But it is observable, that David now when he was most indulgent to himself, and to his own sin, was most severe and even unjust to others; as appears by this passage, and the following relation, ver. 31, which was done in the time of David's impenitent continuance in his sin.
Thus saith the Lord God — Nathan now speaks, not as a petitioner for a poor man, but as an ambassador from the great God.

To be thy wife — To marry her whom he had defiled, and whose husband he had slain, was an affront upon the ordinance of marriage, making that not only to palliate, but in a manner to consecrate such villainies. In all this he despised the word of the Lord; (so it is in the Hebrew.) Not only his commandment in general, but the particular word of promise, which God had before sent him by Nathan, that he would build him an house: which sacred promise if he had had a due value for, he would not have polluted his house with lust and blood.
Never depart — During the residue of thy life.

Own house — From thy own children and family. Thine eyes - Openly, so that thou shalt know it as certainly as if thou didst see it, and yet not be able to hinder it. And give them - I shall by my providence, give him power over them. neighbour - To one who is very near thee. But God expresseth this darkly, that the accomplishment of it might not be hindered.

I have sinned — How serious this confession was, we may see, Psalm li, 1-19. Put away thy sin - That is, so far as concerns thy own life. Not die - As by thy own sentence, ver. 5, thou dost deserve, and may expect to be done by my immediate stroke.

glossa.text: *And Nathan said to David,* etc. ((RAB. ex Euch.)) Yet all the things which were foretold to him for his sin he afterwards endured. God blots out the offence, but does not leave it unavenged. For either a man, repenting, punishes it in himself, or God, taking vengeance for these things, strikes the man. The sin therefore is not spared, because it is not remitted without vengeance. For so David deserved to hear after his confession, *The Lord hath taken away thy sin,* and yet, afflicted afterwards with many torments, in escaping he paid off the guilt of the fault which he had committed. So we are absolved by the wave of salvation from the fault of the first parent, but even when absolved we still die carnally, because God cuts away our offences, either through ourselves or through himself, even when he remits them. For he takes pains to wipe away from his elect by temporal affliction the stains of iniquities, which he does not will to see in them for ever.

notes.text: Thee only — Which is not to be, understood absolutely, because he had sinned against Bathsheba and Uriah, and many others; but comparatively. So the sense is, though I have sinned against my own conscience, and against others; yet nothing is more grievous to me, than that I have sinned against thee. Thy sight - With gross contempt of thee, whom I knew to be a spectator of my most secret actions. Justified - This will be the fruit of my sin, that whatsoever severities thou shalt use towards me, it will be no blemish to thy righteousness, but thy justice will be glorified by all men. Speakest - Hebrew. in thy words, in all thy threatenings denounced against me. Judgest - When thou dost execute thy sentence upon me.

Behold — Nor is this the only sin which I have reason to bewail before thee; for this filthy stream leads me to a corrupt fountain: and upon a review of my heart, I find, that this heinous crime, was the proper fruit of my vile nature, which, ever was, and still is ready to commit ten thousand sins, as occasion offers.

Truth — Uprightness of heart; and this may be added; as an aggravation of the sinfulness of original corruption, because it is contrary to the holy nature and will of God, which requires rectitude of heart: and, as an aggravation of his actual sin, that it was committed against that knowledge, which God had wrote in his heart.

Hyssop — As lepers, are by thy appointment purified by the use of hyssop and other things, so do thou cleanse me a leprous and polluted creature, by thy grace, and by that blood of Christ, which is signified by those ceremonial usages.
Joy — By thy spirit, seal the pardon of my sins on my conscience, which will fill me with joy. Rejoice - That my heart which hath been sorely wounded may be comforted.

Create — Work in me an holy frame of heart, whereby my inward filth may be purged away. Right - Hebrew. firm or constant, that my resolution may be fixed and unmoveable. Spirit - Temper or disposition of soul.

The joy — The comfortable sense of thy saving grace, promised and vouchsafed to me, both for my present and everlasting salvation. Free - Or, ingenuous, or liberal, or princely. Which he seems to oppose to his own base and illiberal and disingenuous and servile spirit, which he had discovered in his wicked practices: a spirit, which may free me from the bondage of sin, and enable me cheerfully to run the way of God's precepts.

glossa.text: *Unto the end, a psalm.* ((CASS.)) When Nathan rebuked him, the king did not blush to confess his sins publicly, etc., *as far as* what avails with God for the penitent. *Of David.* ((AUG.)) He is set forth as an example, not of falling, but of rising again if thou hast fallen, that thou despair not. ((CASS.)) The first thing is entreaty, etc., *as far as* full remission of sins is granted.

*Have mercy on me, O God. ((Ibid.))* This is a penitential psalm, etc., *as far as* because he foresaw that through this psalm many would perish. *According to thy great mercy.* Of a grave sin one would have to despair, were there not a great mercy *misericodia*. A great one cannot be defined, how great it is. *Great mercy. ((Ibid.))* A great mercy brought God down from heaven, etc., *as far as* when God is asked to pardon according to himself? *Of thy tender mercies,* etc. ((CASS.)) He asks through mercy and through tender mercy. And mercy is in the nature, tender mercy in the effect.

*Wash me yet more.* ((CASS.)) What manner of blotting out he would have, he adds: *Cleanse me,* etc. ((HIER.)) So wash that thou make clean; for certain things are washed which nevertheless are not pure.

*For iniquity.* ((AUG., CASS.)) Whose mercy he asks that he may pardon, because he knows him just, that he punishes sins, he adds: Punish thou not, because I punish. *For my iniquity,* etc. *Against me.* ((AUG.)) He had his sin behind his back, when the king gave sentence against the rich man who had seized the poor man's ewe, forgetful of himself.

*To thee only have I sinned.* ((HIER.)) For he alone punishes justly who has not in himself anything that may be reproved; and among men this is Christ alone. *To thee only.* ((CASS.)) Because a king is superior to all, he is to be punished by God alone. *Before thee.* Because he knows that he is everywhere; whence he accuses himself, because in his presence he did not blush to sin. *That thou mayest be justified,* etc. Whose words do not pass away, but are fulfilled. *And mayest overcome when thou art judged.* God is of such great justice *t antae*, etc., *as far as* that he may overcome as between himself and him, if they be judged.

*To thee only.* ((AUG.)) To Christ, who had no sin, etc., *as far as* in that he had so grievously offended God. *And mayest overcome.* ((AUG.)) Or, thou art so just that thou overcomest the devil, and death, and the Jews, when thou art judged: and in the judgment wherein thou wast judged.
*In iniquities.* ((CASS.)) The odium of the sin is lessened, etc., *as far as* he is accused of one and confesses all.

*For behold,* etc. ((AUG.)) He so gives mercy that he keeps truth, so that not even the sins of him whom he pardons are unpunished. For he pardons the man who punishes himself. Mercy therefore it is that a man is set free; truth, that the sin is punished. *Truth,* etc. ((CASS.)) Because in confessing he spoke the truth, which God seeks above sacrifices, he entreats that help be brought him. *The uncertain and hidden things.* ((AUG.)) There are hidden things also, in that to such men, etc., *as far as* whence he had the more to beware of sin. *The hidden things.* ((CASS.)) From the authority of him who makes them manifest, the confidence of washing and of being made white.

*Thou shalt sprinkle me.* ((CASS.)) The second thing is confidence in the mercy of God, which is very profitable: lest despair creep in, which is graver than all sins. *With hyssop. ((Ibid.))* Dipped in the blood of the victim, it was sprinkled over the body of the leper, signifying that the stains of sins are to be washed away by the blood of Christ. ((AUG.)) Hyssop is a lowly herb, etc., *as far as* in which there is a swelling, so humility, pride. *Above snow. ((Ibid.))* Incomparably: whence also on the mountain the garment of Christ shone as snow.
*To my hearing.* ((AUG.)) Mark the humble man. Let me hear thee, etc., *as far as* and because he is now humble, now *the bones that were humbled rejoice.*
*Turn away.* ((CASS.)) Made secure by that confidence, he asks the blotting out of all sins and a full restoration.

*In my bowels. ((Ibid.))* Whence the adultery went forth. In both parts, in soul and in body, he asks the remedy of healing, because in them he sinned. He so desires to be cleansed that he may be seen to wish to commit no such thing further.

notes.text: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord — Imprisoned for his sake and for your sakes; for the sake of the gospel which he had preached amongst them. This was therefore a powerful motive to them to comfort him under it by their obedience.
endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit — That mutual union and harmony, which is a fruit of the Spirit. The bond of peace is love.
There is one body — The universal church, all believers throughout the world. One Spirit, one Lord, one God and Father - The ever-blessed Trinity. One hope - Of heaven.
One outward baptism.
One God and Father of all — That believe. Who is above all - Presiding over all his children, operating through them all by Christ, and dwelling in all by his Spirit.
According to the measure of the gift of Christ — According as Christ is pleased to give to each.

Wherefore he saith — That is, in reference to which God saith by David, Having ascended on high, he led captivity captive - He triumphed over all his enemies, Satan, sin, and death, which had before enslaved all the world: alluding to the custom of ancient conquerors, who led those they had conquered in chains after them. And, as they also used to give donatives to the people, at their return from victory, so he gave gifts to men - Both the ordinary and extraordinary gifts of the Spirit. Psalm lxviii, 18.

Now this expression, He ascended, what is it, but that he descended — That is, does it not imply, that he descended first? Certainly it does, on the supposition of his being God. Otherwise it would not: since all the saints will ascend to heaven, though none of them descended thence. Into the lower parts of the earth - So the womb is called, Psalm cxxxix, 5; the grave, Psalm lxiii, 9.

He that descended — That thus amazingly humbled himself. Is the same that ascended - That was so highly exalted. That he might fill all things - The whole church, with his Spirit, presence, and operations.

And, among other his free gifts, he gave some apostles — His chief ministers and special witnesses, as having seen him after his resurrection, and received their commission immediately from him. And same prophets, and some evangelists - A prophet testifies of things to come; an evangelist of things past: and that chiefly by preaching the gospel before or after any of the apostles. All these were extraordinary officers. The ordinary were. Some pastors - Watching over their several flocks. And some teachers - Whether of the same or a lower order, to assist them, as occasion might require.

In this verse is noted the office of ministers; in the next, the aim of the saints; in the 14th, 15th, 16th, the way of growing in grace. And each of these has three parts, standing in the same order. For the perfecting the saints — The completing them both in number and their various gifts and graces. To the work of the ministry - The serving God and his church in their various ministrations. To the edifying of the body of Christ - The building up this his mystical body in faith, love, holiness.

Till we all — And every one of us. Come to the unity of the faith, and knowledge of the Son of God - To both an exact agreement in the Christian doctrine, and an experimental knowledge of Christ as the Son of God. To a perfect man - To a state of spiritual manhood both in understanding and strength. To the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ - To that maturity of age and spiritual stature wherein we shall be filled with Christ, so that he will be all in all.

Fluctuating to and fro — From within, even when there is no wind. And carried about with every wind - From without; when we are assaulted by others, who are unstable as the wind. By the sleight of men - By their "cogging the dice;" so the original word implies.
Into him — Into his image and Spirit, and into a full union with him.

From whom the whole mystical body fitly joined together — All the parts being fitted for and adapted to each other, and most exactly harmonizing with the whole. And compacted - Knit and cemented together with the utmost firmness. Maketh increase by that which every joint supplieth - Or by the mutual help of every joint. According to the effectual working in the measure of every member - According as every member in its measure effectually works for the support and growth of the whole. A beautiful allusion to the human body, composed of different joints and members, knit together by various ligaments, and furnished with vessels of communication from the head to every part.

glossa.text: *I beseech.* Thus far he has shown that all things are to be attributed to grace, from here he admonishes concerning morals, first all in common, afterward through the several orders.

*In charity. ((AUG.))* For this is the action of the right journey, which always has its eyes toward God. Such action is not broken by business, nor is it turbulent, nor languid, nor bold, nor fugitive, nor headlong, nor prostrate

*In the bond of peace.* That is, keeping peace. And this is peace, if we bear until the last harvest those sins which cannot be rooted out without harm to the wheat, or with hope of the salvation of those to be corrected.

*One Lord.* You ought to keep unity, because we have one Lord, not three, for whose diverse wills you should have to be at variance. And you are bidden to believe the same, and to work in the same manner. And you have one God, the creator of all and father by his providing: and therefore no one can prefer himself to another. *Who,* that is, God, *is above all,* that is, he excels all creatures, whose dignity should invite you, *and through all things* diffused, because he is everywhere, and therefore to be feared; since he can nowhere be avoided. *And in us all,* through grace, we who keep unity. And so this is taken not singularly of one person, but commonly of all, that is, of the Trinity. *One faith.* Not in number, but in kind, because it is alike in all.

*He led captivity captive.* That is, those whom the devil had led captive from paradise, and had made the proper goods of the world and of hell, Christ made captive again, while they are led back to heaven.

*Prophets ((AMBR.))* In the New Testament the expounders of the Scriptures are called prophets, yet there were certain in the first beginning of the faith who foretold things to come, as Agabus, and the seven daughters of Philip.

*Evangelists.* Who are also deacons, because although they are not priests, yet they can preach the gospel.

*Unto the work of the ministry.* And these he gave unto the work of the ministry, that each might fully be able to do the work of the ministration committed to him. For if one man had all things, he would not perfectly perform each. *Unto the consummation.* That is, that he might consummate those who are already holy. *And unto the edification.* That is, that they may build into the body of Christ those who are as yet strangers.

*Until.* That is, in the *day* of judgment. *All.* We who are in one and not discrepant faith: and in one and not differing unity *of the knowledge of the Son of God;* or in the virtues by which the Son of God is known in us; or by which we shall know him in the time to come. *Let us meet.* One another, from the diverse parts of the world, or Christ himself, as it were running with desire unto joy. *Unto a perfect man.* That each one may be a perfect man and having the same age, which is the measure and the limit of age, beyond which nothing accrues naturally to a man: in which age Christ had the fullness of years and of body, in which he passed out of this world. For all shall rise again in that same age in which Christ died and rose again, of whatever age they shall have died.
*Christ.* He is called Anointed. And in the Old Testament the kings were anointed.

notes.text: Our Lord does not satisfy their curiosity, but corrects the wrong motive they had in seeking him: because ye did eat — Merely for temporal advantage. Hitherto Christ had been gathering hearers: he now begins to try their sincerity, by a figurative discourse concerning his passion, and the fruit of it, to be received by faith.

labour not for the meat which perisheth — For bodily food: not for that only not chiefly: not at all, but in subordination to grace, faith, love, the meat which endureth to everlasting life. labour, work for this; foreverlasting life. So our Lord expressly commands, work for life, as well as from life: from a principle of faith and love. Him hath the Father sealed - By this very miracle, as well as by his whole testimony concerning him. See chap. iii, 33. Sealing is a mark of the authenticity of a writing.
The works of God — Works pleasing to God.
This is the work of God — The work most pleasing to God, and the foundation of all others: that ye believe - He expresses it first properly, afterward figuratively.
What sign dost thou? — Amazing, after what they had just seen!

Our fathers ate manna — This sign Moses gave them. He gave them bread from heaven - From the lower sublunary heaven; to which Jesus opposes the highest heaven: in which sense he says seven times, ver. 32, 33, 38, 50, 58, 62, that he himself came down from heaven.
Moses gave you not bread from heaven — It was not Moses who gave the manna to your fathers; but my Father who now giveth the true bread from heaven. Psalm lxxviii, 24.

He that — giveth life to the world - Not (like the manna) to one people only: and that from generation to generation. Our Lord does not yet say, I am that bread; else the Jews would not have given him so respectful an answer, ver. 34.
Give us this bread — Meaning it still, in a literal sense: yet they seem now to be not far from believing.
I am the bread of life — Having and giving life: he that cometh -he that believeth - Equivalent expressions: shall never hunger, thirst - Shall be satisfied, happy, forever.

glossa.text: *And when they had found him.* Behold, he is present to those from whom he had fled, lest they should make him king. Why then had he fled, if not for the aforesaid sacrament? Again, being present, he speaks to them, that of those whose bellies he filled, he may fill the minds also, saying: *Amen, amen I say to you,* teaching those whom he appointed teachers to flee praise and earthly rule, but nevertheless to press on in preaching.

*Amen, amen I say to you.* After he had treated of his divinity, by which he is the same with the Father and to be honoured with the same honour, and of his humanity, by which he frees from death and raises up, being worthy of great honour, he wishes to treat of the food of life, that is, of the Word of God. And this is the connection as regards the sense. But according to the letter, thus: You seek me, not for my own sake, but for the sake of the loaves that perish. Therefore work, that is, seek me for my own sake, not for the sake of anything else. For he himself is that food which endures unto life everlasting, as he will afterwards say openly. In like manner many seek Jesus daily, not for Jesus' sake, but that it may be well with them in this time.

*God hath sealed.* As by a proper sign he marked him off from the rest, because he who is the Son of man is also the Son of God; and therefore do not despise me, the Son of man, but ask of me spiritual food.

*This is the work of God.* Faith working by love is the work, because if the means be wanting, nothing is required but the will. Deservedly also is that faith called a work which works by love, which is the beginning and the end of all good.

*He said therefore.* Because they preferred the work of Moses to his work, he shows that that was the less, since it was not bread from heaven but only a figure of it, and that his own is the greater, which is the bread from heaven that gives life; and this is the food which he said above endures unto life everlasting.

*For the true bread.* The angels eat the pure Word, solid food; but we the Word, yet turned into milk, because if we cannot eat, we can suck. For unless he were made flesh, he would not be known by us, he would not be tasted by us.

*Lord, always,* etc. As the Samaritan woman, hearing: *He that shall drink of this water shall not thirst for ever,* took it according to the body, and yet, wishing to be without labour and want, said: *Give me this water,* so these seek a bread which may refresh them and never fail, on account of which they wished to make him king. But Jesus calls them back to himself, and more evidently opens what bread he spoke of: *I am the bread of life.* I shall be able to give life, because I am the bread that gives life, baked and formed by the fire of the Holy Spirit in the oven of the virginal womb, and given to the world to drive away the hunger of the ignorance of God.

notes.text: That they should gather a double portion on the sixth day, ver. 22-26.
That they should expect none on the seventh day, ver. 27-31,

That they should preserve a pot of it for a memorial, ver 32.

1. A month's provision, it seems, the host of Israel took with them out of Egypt, when they came thence on the 15th day of the first month, which, by the 15th day of the second month, was all spent.

2. Then the whole congregation murmured against Moses and Aaron - God's viceregents among them.

3. They so undervalue their deliverance, that they wish, they had died in Egypt, nay, and died by the hand of the Lord too. That is, by some of the plagues which cut off the Egyptians; as if it were not the hand of the Lord, but of Moses only, that brought them into this wilderness. 'Tis common for people to say of that pain, or sickness, which they see not second causes of, It is what pleaseth God, as if that were not so likewise which comes by the hand of man, or some visible accident. We cannot suppose they had any great plenty in Egypt, how largely soever they now talk of the flesh-pots, nor could they fear dying for want in the wilderness while they had their flocks and herds with them; but discontent magnifies what is past, and vilifies what is present, without regard to truth or reason. None talk more absurdly than murmurers.

4. Man being made out of the earth, his Maker has wisely ordered him food out of the earth, Psalm civ, 14. But the people of Israel typifying the church of the first-born that are written in heaven, receiving their charters, laws and commissions from heaven, from heaven also they received their food. See what God designed in making this provision for them, that I may prove them whether they will walk in my law or no - Whether they will trust me, and whether they would serve him, and be ever faithful to so good a master.

glossa.text:
*And all the congregation of Israel murmured,* etc. ((ORIG., homil. 7 in Exod.)) O ungrateful people! it desires Egypt, it that saw the Egyptians destroyed; and the flesh of Egypt, it that sees the flesh of the Egyptians given both to the fishes and to the birds! It murmurs against Moses, nay rather against God; but the first time pardon is granted, and the second, and perhaps the third: but if they do not cease, but persist, hear what follows, it is related in the book of Numbers ((Num. XXI)), and the same Apostle rehearses it, saying ((I Cor. X)): *Neither do you murmur, as some of them murmured, and perished by the serpents. These things were written on account of us, upon whom the ends of the world are come.* But if we do not cease to murmur and complain against God, we shall incur a like peril of offence, or a like example of it. For when we lay the blame upon the inclemency of the heavens, the unfruitfulness of the crops, the rarity of showers, and upon the prosperity of some and the unprosperity of others, we murmur against God. But these things are pardoned at first, and are severely avenged upon those who persist, because serpents shall be sent upon them, that is, they shall be handed over to unclean and poisonous spirits, which by hidden bites feed upon the inner chambers of the heart.

((ORIG.)) For the correction of those who read, the sin of the people is set down: that it murmured and was ungrateful for the divine benefits, when it had received the heavenly manna. In the second month, on the fifteenth day of the month, which is not written without reason. Recall the laws of the pasch which were spoken ((Num. IX)), and thou wilt find there that this is the time which is appointed for the keeping of a second pasch by those who have been unclean in soul, or taken up with business abroad. Those who had not been unclean in soul, or were not journeying far off, kept the pasch on the fourteenth day of the first month; but those far off on pilgrimage, and the unclean, keep the second pasch at this time, in which the manna came down from heaven. On the day on which the first pasch is kept, the manna does not come down, but on that on which the second is kept: the first pasch is that of the Jewish people; the second is ours. For we were unclean in soul, we who *worshipped idols; and we were pilgrims, and far off, strangers and pilgrims from the testaments of God,* etc. ((Eph. II.)) But manna is given from heaven, not on the day on which the first pasch is kept, but on that on which the second is: *For the bread which came down from heaven ((Joan. VI))* did not come to those who were celebrating the first solemnity, but to us, who have received the second. *For Christ our pasch is sacrificed, who as true man came down as bread from heaven ((I Cor. V.))* Let us see meanwhile what is shown to have been done on this day: On the fourteenth day of the second month the people murmured, etc.
*We sat over the fleshpots,* etc. They had flocks of sheep and herds of oxen, of which they could eat; but they burned with desire for the fish and the fowl in which Egypt abounds.

*Behold I will rain,* etc. ((ORIG., homil. 8 in Exod.)) I should wish first to have a discourse upon this scripture with the Jews, to whom the oracles of God were entrusted, as to what seems to them of that which it says: *For six days together you shall gather, but on the sixth day double.* It appears therefore that that day is named the sixth which is set before the sabbath; but the sabbath is the seventh day. I ask therefore on what day the manna began to be given? and I wish to compare our Lord's day with the sabbath of the Jews. For from Scripture it appears that on the Lord's day the manna is first given, gathered for six days together; on the seventh, which is the sabbath, there is a ceasing. Since therefore on the Lord's day God rained manna, and not on the sabbath, let the Jews understand that even then our Lord's day was preferred to their sabbath; and it was signified that on that day the grace of God did not come down from heaven to them, and that the heavenly bread, which is the word of God, did not reach them; whence Osee III: *For many days the children of Israel shall sit without king, without prince, without victim, without sacrifice, without priest.* But on our Lord's day the Lord always rains manna, that is, the heavenly words which are joyful to us. Those unhappy men sigh even after manna as their fathers did, and do not deserve to receive it; for they cannot eat what is small like coriander seed, and white like hoar frost. For they perceive nothing in the word of God that is small, subtle and spiritual, but all of it fat and gross. *For the heart of this people is grown gross.* The interpretation also of this name sounds thus. For manna is interpreted *What is this?* The very force of the name invites to learning, so that when thou hearest the law of God recited, thou mayest always inquire and say to the teachers, *What is this?* Thou therefore, if thou wilt eat manna, and receive the word of God, know that it is small and very subtle, like coriander seed: for it has somewhat of the herb whereby it can nourish and refresh the weak. *For he that is weak eateth herbs ((Rom. XIV))*. For it has also somewhat of sharpness, and therefore is as hoar frost; but of whiteness and sweetness very much. What is whiter, more splendid, than divine learning? what sweeter, more delightful, than the words of God, which are above honey and the honeycomb?

*Loaves.* The manna, namely: it is a manner of speech by which bread is put for food; and Scripture loves rather to say *loaves* in the plural than *bread* in the singular.

*That I may prove.* This proving is a testing, not a seducing to sin; nor are they proved for this reason, that God did not know: but he shows them to themselves, that they may become the more humble in asking help and in acknowledging the grace of God.

notes.text: Heaven — Which he compares to a store-house, whereof God shuts or opens the doors, as he sees fit.
Angels food — Manna, so called, because it was made by the ministry of angels.
South wind — First an eastern, and afterwards a southern wind.
Fowl — But God took away from them the use of their wings, and made them to fall into the hands of the Israelites.

glossa.text: *And he commanded.* Both were set down briefly, namely that he heard, and that wrath went up; here he begins to tell it openly. And first he follows out how he heard, afterwards in the following part how he took vengeance. *And the gates of heaven.* ((CASS.)) The gates are the preachers themselves, by whom entry is made into heaven; or the Scriptures. *He opened.* Because he gave his Spirit to his own, that they might understand the Scriptures.

*Manna to eat.* ((AUG.)) It signifies the bread which came down from heaven, which is the food of angels: which, that man might eat it, *the Word was made flesh ((Joan. I))*, who is rained upon the whole world through the evangelical clouds, and, their hearts being opened as heavenly gates, is preached to the believing Church, not to the tempting Synagogue. ((CASS.)) *Manna, what is this?* because this food is sought after with wonder, and is known to be the body of Christ. *The bread of heaven.* ((ID.)) No other than Christ, by whom the heavenly ones, that is the angels, are refreshed in the contemplation of him; and this bread, that is the Word, on which great food the angels are fed, made milk through the flesh, man eats.
*The south-west wind.* Because the quails are there.

*And he rained upon them,* etc. ((AUG.)) So also a little faith, etc., *as far as* whence: *If I have told you earthly things, and you believe me not, how, if I tell you heavenly things?* etc. ((Joan. III.)) 

*As dust.* ((CASS.)) *Dust* here signifies the subtlety of understanding, which climbs to the things above. *Sand,* the countless abundance of prudence seasoned with the savour of salt. *Feathered fowls.* Heavenly desires, on which the soul is fed and grows fat: these we can receive within the enclosures of the Church, whence he adds:

*And they fell in the midst of their camp.* ((AUG.)) Signifying by this that the winds come of their own accord to men, and carry to them the words divinely sent, that they may hear them in their own seats, and about their tents: because their sound went out into all the earth.
*And they did eat.* They were convicted, who had thought this impossible to God.

notes.text: I therefore, the prisoner of the Lord — Imprisoned for his sake and for your sakes; for the sake of the gospel which he had preached amongst them. This was therefore a powerful motive to them to comfort him under it by their obedience.
endeavouring to keep the unity of the Spirit — That mutual union and harmony, which is a fruit of the Spirit. The bond of peace is love.
There is one body — The universal church, all believers throughout the world. One Spirit, one Lord, one God and Father - The ever-blessed Trinity. One hope - Of heaven.
One outward baptism.
One God and Father of all — That believe. Who is above all - Presiding over all his children, operating through them all by Christ, and dwelling in all by his Spirit.
According to the measure of the gift of Christ — According as Christ is pleased to give to each.

Wherefore he saith — That is, in reference to which God saith by David, Having ascended on high, he led captivity captive - He triumphed over all his enemies, Satan, sin, and death, which had before enslaved all the world: alluding to the custom of ancient conquerors, who led those they had conquered in chains after them. And, as they also used to give donatives to the people, at their return from victory, so he gave gifts to men - Both the ordinary and extraordinary gifts of the Spirit. Psalm lxviii, 18.

Now this expression, He ascended, what is it, but that he descended — That is, does it not imply, that he descended first? Certainly it does, on the supposition of his being God. Otherwise it would not: since all the saints will ascend to heaven, though none of them descended thence. Into the lower parts of the earth - So the womb is called, Psalm cxxxix, 5; the grave, Psalm lxiii, 9.

He that descended — That thus amazingly humbled himself. Is the same that ascended - That was so highly exalted. That he might fill all things - The whole church, with his Spirit, presence, and operations.

And, among other his free gifts, he gave some apostles — His chief ministers and special witnesses, as having seen him after his resurrection, and received their commission immediately from him. And same prophets, and some evangelists - A prophet testifies of things to come; an evangelist of things past: and that chiefly by preaching the gospel before or after any of the apostles. All these were extraordinary officers. The ordinary were. Some pastors - Watching over their several flocks. And some teachers - Whether of the same or a lower order, to assist them, as occasion might require.

In this verse is noted the office of ministers; in the next, the aim of the saints; in the 14th, 15th, 16th, the way of growing in grace. And each of these has three parts, standing in the same order. For the perfecting the saints — The completing them both in number and their various gifts and graces. To the work of the ministry - The serving God and his church in their various ministrations. To the edifying of the body of Christ - The building up this his mystical body in faith, love, holiness.

Till we all — And every one of us. Come to the unity of the faith, and knowledge of the Son of God - To both an exact agreement in the Christian doctrine, and an experimental knowledge of Christ as the Son of God. To a perfect man - To a state of spiritual manhood both in understanding and strength. To the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ - To that maturity of age and spiritual stature wherein we shall be filled with Christ, so that he will be all in all.

Fluctuating to and fro — From within, even when there is no wind. And carried about with every wind - From without; when we are assaulted by others, who are unstable as the wind. By the sleight of men - By their "cogging the dice;" so the original word implies.
Into him — Into his image and Spirit, and into a full union with him.

From whom the whole mystical body fitly joined together — All the parts being fitted for and adapted to each other, and most exactly harmonizing with the whole. And compacted - Knit and cemented together with the utmost firmness. Maketh increase by that which every joint supplieth - Or by the mutual help of every joint. According to the effectual working in the measure of every member - According as every member in its measure effectually works for the support and growth of the whole. A beautiful allusion to the human body, composed of different joints and members, knit together by various ligaments, and furnished with vessels of communication from the head to every part.

glossa.text: *I beseech.* Thus far he has shown that all things are to be attributed to grace, from here he admonishes concerning morals, first all in common, afterward through the several orders.

*In charity. ((AUG.))* For this is the action of the right journey, which always has its eyes toward God. Such action is not broken by business, nor is it turbulent, nor languid, nor bold, nor fugitive, nor headlong, nor prostrate

*In the bond of peace.* That is, keeping peace. And this is peace, if we bear until the last harvest those sins which cannot be rooted out without harm to the wheat, or with hope of the salvation of those to be corrected.

*One Lord.* You ought to keep unity, because we have one Lord, not three, for whose diverse wills you should have to be at variance. And you are bidden to believe the same, and to work in the same manner. And you have one God, the creator of all and father by his providing: and therefore no one can prefer himself to another. *Who,* that is, God, *is above all,* that is, he excels all creatures, whose dignity should invite you, *and through all things* diffused, because he is everywhere, and therefore to be feared; since he can nowhere be avoided. *And in us all,* through grace, we who keep unity. And so this is taken not singularly of one person, but commonly of all, that is, of the Trinity. *One faith.* Not in number, but in kind, because it is alike in all.

*He led captivity captive.* That is, those whom the devil had led captive from paradise, and had made the proper goods of the world and of hell, Christ made captive again, while they are led back to heaven.

*Prophets ((AMBR.))* In the New Testament the expounders of the Scriptures are called prophets, yet there were certain in the first beginning of the faith who foretold things to come, as Agabus, and the seven daughters of Philip.

*Evangelists.* Who are also deacons, because although they are not priests, yet they can preach the gospel.

*Unto the work of the ministry.* And these he gave unto the work of the ministry, that each might fully be able to do the work of the ministration committed to him. For if one man had all things, he would not perfectly perform each. *Unto the consummation.* That is, that he might consummate those who are already holy. *And unto the edification.* That is, that they may build into the body of Christ those who are as yet strangers.

*Until.* That is, in the *day* of judgment. *All.* We who are in one and not discrepant faith: and in one and not differing unity *of the knowledge of the Son of God;* or in the virtues by which the Son of God is known in us; or by which we shall know him in the time to come. *Let us meet.* One another, from the diverse parts of the world, or Christ himself, as it were running with desire unto joy. *Unto a perfect man.* That each one may be a perfect man and having the same age, which is the measure and the limit of age, beyond which nothing accrues naturally to a man: in which age Christ had the fullness of years and of body, in which he passed out of this world. For all shall rise again in that same age in which Christ died and rose again, of whatever age they shall have died.
*Christ.* He is called Anointed. And in the Old Testament the kings were anointed.

notes.text: Our Lord does not satisfy their curiosity, but corrects the wrong motive they had in seeking him: because ye did eat — Merely for temporal advantage. Hitherto Christ had been gathering hearers: he now begins to try their sincerity, by a figurative discourse concerning his passion, and the fruit of it, to be received by faith.

labour not for the meat which perisheth — For bodily food: not for that only not chiefly: not at all, but in subordination to grace, faith, love, the meat which endureth to everlasting life. labour, work for this; foreverlasting life. So our Lord expressly commands, work for life, as well as from life: from a principle of faith and love. Him hath the Father sealed - By this very miracle, as well as by his whole testimony concerning him. See chap. iii, 33. Sealing is a mark of the authenticity of a writing.
The works of God — Works pleasing to God.
This is the work of God — The work most pleasing to God, and the foundation of all others: that ye believe - He expresses it first properly, afterward figuratively.
What sign dost thou? — Amazing, after what they had just seen!

Our fathers ate manna — This sign Moses gave them. He gave them bread from heaven - From the lower sublunary heaven; to which Jesus opposes the highest heaven: in which sense he says seven times, ver. 32, 33, 38, 50, 58, 62, that he himself came down from heaven.
Moses gave you not bread from heaven — It was not Moses who gave the manna to your fathers; but my Father who now giveth the true bread from heaven. Psalm lxxviii, 24.

He that — giveth life to the world - Not (like the manna) to one people only: and that from generation to generation. Our Lord does not yet say, I am that bread; else the Jews would not have given him so respectful an answer, ver. 34.
Give us this bread — Meaning it still, in a literal sense: yet they seem now to be not far from believing.
I am the bread of life — Having and giving life: he that cometh -he that believeth - Equivalent expressions: shall never hunger, thirst - Shall be satisfied, happy, forever.

glossa.text: *And when they had found him.* Behold, he is present to those from whom he had fled, lest they should make him king. Why then had he fled, if not for the aforesaid sacrament? Again, being present, he speaks to them, that of those whose bellies he filled, he may fill the minds also, saying: *Amen, amen I say to you,* teaching those whom he appointed teachers to flee praise and earthly rule, but nevertheless to press on in preaching.

*Amen, amen I say to you.* After he had treated of his divinity, by which he is the same with the Father and to be honoured with the same honour, and of his humanity, by which he frees from death and raises up, being worthy of great honour, he wishes to treat of the food of life, that is, of the Word of God. And this is the connection as regards the sense. But according to the letter, thus: You seek me, not for my own sake, but for the sake of the loaves that perish. Therefore work, that is, seek me for my own sake, not for the sake of anything else. For he himself is that food which endures unto life everlasting, as he will afterwards say openly. In like manner many seek Jesus daily, not for Jesus' sake, but that it may be well with them in this time.

*God hath sealed.* As by a proper sign he marked him off from the rest, because he who is the Son of man is also the Son of God; and therefore do not despise me, the Son of man, but ask of me spiritual food.

*This is the work of God.* Faith working by love is the work, because if the means be wanting, nothing is required but the will. Deservedly also is that faith called a work which works by love, which is the beginning and the end of all good.

*He said therefore.* Because they preferred the work of Moses to his work, he shows that that was the less, since it was not bread from heaven but only a figure of it, and that his own is the greater, which is the bread from heaven that gives life; and this is the food which he said above endures unto life everlasting.

*For the true bread.* The angels eat the pure Word, solid food; but we the Word, yet turned into milk, because if we cannot eat, we can suck. For unless he were made flesh, he would not be known by us, he would not be tasted by us.

*Lord, always,* etc. As the Samaritan woman, hearing: *He that shall drink of this water shall not thirst for ever,* took it according to the body, and yet, wishing to be without labour and want, said: *Give me this water,* so these seek a bread which may refresh them and never fail, on account of which they wished to make him king. But Jesus calls them back to himself, and more evidently opens what bread he spoke of: *I am the bread of life.* I shall be able to give life, because I am the bread that gives life, baked and formed by the fire of the Holy Spirit in the oven of the virginal womb, and given to the world to drive away the hunger of the ignorance of God.

Lead on, O cloud of Presence

registers.label: Spare
lines: Do not work for the bread that perishes.
Give us the bread that lasts to eternal life.
I am the bread of life, says the Lord.
Whoever comes to him will never hunger again.
Create in us a clean heart, O God.
Renew a right spirit within us.
Come, all who hunger; come, let us worship.
We come to the bread of life. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: The crowd hunts him down the next morning, still tasting yesterday's bread, and he says: do not work for food that spoils.
Give us this bread always.
What our ancestors ate in the wilderness kept them one more day; this bread comes down from heaven and gives life to the world.
Give us this bread always.
I am the bread of life, he says; whoever comes to me will never be hungry, whoever believes will never be thirsty again.
Give us this bread always.
So bring the hunger underneath your hunger, the thirst no cup has touched; here is the One your soul was made for.
Give us this bread always.
